matches.quote: That is only true after dropping the symmetry-allowed kx·ky·kz ẑ term... Including this term would allow dispersive Andreev bound states on (001).
The fitted gaps are anomalously large... roughly 3.7 times the BCS value... Discuss the magnitudes against independent spectroscopic gap estimates (e.g., STM, refs. 26 and 34).
B₂u and B₃u are indistinguishable for an (001) junction... Use field orientation to separate B₂u from B₃u... Add a second junction orientation.
Pressure gradients are already invoked to explain the double dips, so they should be quantified, for example through the width of the manometer transition.
The fitted Γ values (0.1–0.4 meV, i.e., Γ/Δ up to ~0.5) would wash out the predicted splitting. An anisotropic Au state... is never fitted.

The discrimination among irreducible representations is not quantitative and depends on model truncations... Until then, "unambiguously suggesting the presence of pz component" (p. 4) should be softened.
The expected low-T state is a two-component state such as B₂u + iB₃u, which may be non-unitary... Model a two-component state.
The model uses a single spherical Fermi surface. UTe₂ has quasi-2D cylindrical sheets along c... so the quantitative Δz/Δx ratio is model-dependent.
Sub-unity dips at finite bias... are a well-known signature of... critical current... no field dependence is shown under pressure at all... Dip position versus T and versus H
Pressure evolution may reflect contact evolution... Γ falls from 0.39 to 0.10 meV... lowering Γ at a fixed ratio Δz/Δx = 0.55 produces pronounced side features
The number of channels and the per-channel free parameters... are not stated... justify the number of channels, for example with an information criterion.
A wholesale IR switch conflicts with Landau theory. At a second-order transition... the low-T phase generically retains the high-T component.
The superposition model (Eqs. 2–3) is under-specified... ⟨Δz⟩/⟨Δx(y)⟩ is an average over different local states, and its physical meaning is unclear.
So is a broad flat-topped peak flanked by sharp dips, as at 1.4 GPa (Fig. 3d)... Fits at 1.0 GPa... and at 1.4 GPa are not shown.
All pressure data come from a single soft contact on sample S1... Show the spectrum after pressure release... measure at least one additional contact or sample under pressure.
The manuscript does not report: the normal-state contact resistance... an estimate of contact size (e.g., via a Wexler analysis...)... which transport regime the contact is in.
Table S1 has the Δz and Δx(y) column headers swapped... As printed, the table implies a ratio greater than 1, contradicting the 0.57(5) quoted in the text.
Provide χ² maps or confidence regions in the (Δz/Δx, Γ, Z) space, to expose parameter correlations. Error bars of ±0.01 meV... seem implausibly small
State whether any parameters were held fixed versus temperature.

notes: C16 is marked partly because the referee dismisses pressure inhomogeneity in Daphne 7373 as small, whereas the review asks to quantify gradients and questions the physical meaning of the averaged ratio under inhomogeneity. C5 is marked partly because the review proposes modeling a chiral B2u+iB3u state for SC3 via Landau theory rather than directly asking if PCS can detect TRSB/chirality. C17 is marked partly because the review critiques the physical meaning and mathematical form of the linear superposition model (Eqs. 2-3) without specifically framing it as neglected interband coupling. C19 is marked partly because the review notices the identical Γ and Z values across temperatures in Figs. S7-S8 and asks whether they were held fixed vs T.
